facts.fact: Central African Republic's delegate said a digitalisation process backed by the European Union is at pilot phase and should extend to 40 localities in 2025.

The DGDEC director general told the July 2026 EGMRG meeting that the national civil-registry database (RNEC) holds more than 225,000 birth records, that digitisation of civil-registry documents is under way, that a 45-centre operational map is validated and that an integrated Central African civil-registry software is in development, with EU/CIVIPOL MODERO support.

note: Digitisation of civil-registry documents at Bossangoa is only a stated next step (IT equipment and training); no digital register is procured, piloted or in service.

facts.fact: Ya Ca News reports 28 officers from the civil registration centres of Bangui, Bimbo and Begoua, the National Archives and the Tribunals were trained on 11-13 November 2026 to digitise and index acts in the Digital Archives module of the civil status software (LGEC).

Oubangui Médias reports that the MODERO steering committee, meeting on 17 November 2026, named the civil-status management software MbetiNet and adopted a function for collecting civil-status data in the platform and app, with 130,000 acts digitised in January-September 2026.

The civil-status software MbetiNet, which records births, marriages and deaths, is being piloted at Bimbo commune's main civil-status centre, with teams deployed from 16 November 2026 under the EU-funded MODERO project run by CIVIPOL.
